question_type: Average YoY growth plus log-linear OLS (slope, intercept on a fiscal-year index) of one agency's annual outlays, FY2007-FY2013, stitched from several issues

opus_path.decision: Mapped 'total on-budget and off-budget outlays' for the Judicial Branch to the FFO-3 table 'On-Budget and Off-Budget Outlays by Agency', column 'Judicial branch (2)', millions; 7 fiscal years -> 6 YoY rates, arithmetic mean (not CAGR); flagged the fiscal-year-index origin (0, 1 or calendar year) as an ambiguity affecting only the intercept.
No issue pinned -> latest published vintage. Noticed each FFO-3 printing carries only 5 actual fiscal years, so FY2007/FY2008 must come from earlier issues.
Grepped case-insensitively for 'judicial' (the table uses lowercase 'Judicial branch'), found the FFO-3 header and a separate FFO-4 'Judicial branch' row.
Looped over every issue 2007_03..2016_12, pulled the Judicial column from FFO-3 annual rows, tabulated first prints vs revised values per year and took the stable latest revision for each year.

Explicitly rejected FFO-4 'Summary of Receipts by Source and Outlays by Agency' (Total funds column), whose FY2013 Judicial cell differs from FFO-3 by one unit (fund-group sum rounding), because FFO-3's title matches the question wording.
calc.py asserts every hard-coded cell against the corpus line it cites, then computes the mean YoY and OLS for all three index conventions in one run; chose t=1..7 (FY2007=1).
Sensitivity analysis (first-print vintage, FFO-4 value, CAGR) plus an adversarial reviewer that re-opened the source lines and recomputed in pure Python.

opus_key_moves: Chose FFO-3 because its title literally matches the question phrase and explicitly rejected the FFO-4 'Total funds' cell that differs by one unit in FY2013
Computed every convention (index origin 0/1/year, first-print vs revised) in one script that also asserted each cited cell, so the chosen convention and number could not drift apart
Committed once after a single scripted computation and an independent review

first_divergence.what_glm_did: Had the correct FFO-3 series and the correct candidate (1-based index, printed by its own script at [26], chosen at [27]), but did not commit. It entered a 3-command cycle (read 2012_09 lines 680-750, FTS search for the phrase 'fiscal year index', FTS search for 'TABLE FFO-3 Judicial branch') repeated ~23 times each, until the Codex context was compacted ([169]). After compaction it re-verified from a handoff note: heredoc failed [172], the relative corpus path was wrong [172], python3 hit the Xcode shim [177], so it hand-wrote an awk OLS at [180] using x=i-1 (a 0-based index) while its reasoning at [178] said the index is 1..7. At [181] it noticed the awk intercept disagreed with the handoff's (correct) value and resolved the conflict by mental arithmetic that mis-estimated the mean of ln(outlays), 'confirming' the buggy awk value.
first_divergence.what_opus_did: Computed all index conventions in one asserted script, picked 1-based, and committed after review; no repeated actions, no recomputation outside the script.
first_divergence.why_glm_went_that_way: No visible reason for the loop: the repeated THINK lines ([33]/[35]/[37] ...) are verbatim copies, i.e. degenerate repetition rather than a deliberate search. After compaction, the model trusted a fresh (buggy) recomputation over its own pre-compaction result ('Handoff says ... maybe error' at [181]).
first_divergence.consequence: Submitted the 0-based intercept (shifted by exactly one slope unit, ~0.3% off) with the correct YoY and slope; 587 s, 91 requests, 10.7 M input tokens.

secondary_errors.note: Proximate cause: awk loop set x=i-1 (0..6) although the stated convention was 1..7; the mental cross-check at [181] claimed '1..7 gives' the awk value, based on a wrong estimate of the mean of the logs. A script printing both conventions side by side would have exposed it.
Post-compaction tool friction: heredoc temp-file denial, relative corpus path that does not exist in the workspace, python3 Xcode shim; this pushed it to ad-hoc awk.

remedies.intervention: Repeated-action breaker: if the same shell command (normalized) runs 3 times, block it and force a commit of the current best candidate (or a reviewer turn).
remedies.why: Three commands each ran ~23 times after a correct candidate existed at [26]-[27]; breaking at the 3rd repeat (~[42]) would have committed before compaction.

remedies.intervention: Compaction-proof candidate ledger (value, convention, cited cells, script path) written as soon as a candidate is computed; after compaction a disagreeing recomputation must be reconciled by re-running both conventions in one script, never by mental arithmetic.
remedies.why: At [181] the handoff held the correct value; the actor overrode it with a buggy awk plus a wrong mental check.

remedies.intervention: A working calculation path: a stats helper (ols(y, x) that echoes the x vector) or a writable script file runner that avoids heredoc/python3 shim failures.
remedies.why: The awk fallback at [180] was forced by heredoc and python3 failures at [172]/[177]; an echoed x vector would have shown 0..6.

remedies.intervention: Final-answer recompute check: re-run the computation from the cited cells with the convention the actor declared in its reasoning ('index 1..7') and block submission on mismatch.
remedies.why: The declared convention at [178] and the implemented one at [180] disagreed; a convention-to-code check catches exactly this.

right_arms_note: none: found FFO-3 by listing the FFO table titles in 2014_03 ([21]) after rejecting FFO-4 as 'monthly not annual' ([20]), took FY2007-FY2008 from the 2012_03 annual rows and FY2009-FY2013 from 2014_03, chose the 1-based index at [26] and committed immediately at [32] (14 requests, no loop, no adapter pulling it toward FFO-4).
text_vs_mechanism: Cards failed because of text (an over-broad card), so a scoped card would plausibly fix it, though a title-match check is more robust. The prompt arm already had 'commit as soon as a candidate exists' and 'do not loop' as text and still looped ~135 steps into a compaction, so its failure needs mechanisms: a loop breaker/forced commit (CONTROL) and a compaction-proof candidate ledger (STATE).
notes: Two different failure modes on one question: adapter-induced source choice (cards) and a pure episode-control failure (prompt). The prompt learner's follow-up lesson (1-based index) misattributes the cause: the actor intended 1-based and implemented 0-based after compaction. A postmortem that diffs the declared convention against the executed code would diagnose this correctly. The deck header's 'follow a matching card' plus keyword triggers makes cards act as overriding evidence; the actor treated card text as more authoritative than a literal title match it had itself observed.
